content.title: Jennifer Lawrence bids farewell to The Hunger Games - NZ Herald
content.text: SearchWatch live: Finance Minister Nicola Willis delivers economic updateSubscribeSign InAdvertisementAdvertise with NZME.Jennifer Lawrence was Forbes' best-paid actress of 2015 with $76.8 million in earnings. Photo / APJennifer Lawrence is bidding farewell to The Hunger Games, the wildly popular fantasy franchise that made her a megastar and rare Hollywood action heroine. Lawrence is back as bow-and-arrow badass Katniss Everdeen leading her rebels deeper into the fight against injustice in their dystopian world in The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2, opening around the globe between November 18-20. But the movie marks the final chapter in the hugely successful saga that saw Lawrence - at 25 already an Oscar winner and the world's highest-paid actress - catapulted to fame."I think it will be pretty bizarre when the movie is finally out and ... everything is officially done," said Lawrence. "This movie has been my life for so many years."The series, adapted from the teen novels of Suzanne Collins, tells the story of Everdeen's battle to survive in a reality TV-style life-and-death game in a post-apocalyptic future. Lawrence said it took her a while to adapt to her new life in the spotlight amid the massive Hunger Games success - and the pressure that accompanied it."There were a few years of getting used to it, your entire world changes," she said.Fans the world over have embraced The Hunger Games since the first film came out in 2012, with the franchise passing the billion-dollar mark at the box office.Trailer: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2 ...Video Player is loading.Play Video HideThis is a modal window. "But the pressure ... you just can't think about it."Discover moreEntertainmentWhy is JLaw's Joy trailer so confusing?27 Oct 11:30 PMEntertainmentBox office heavyweights fight it out01 Nov 04:00 PMEntertainmentHunger Games stars leave mark on Hollywood01 Nov 09:20 PMOpinionLet's review Lena Dunham's feminist newsletter03 Nov 06:00 PMThe blockbusters have gone down in history for having a female heroine leading the fight.AdvertisementAdvertise with NZME.But "it's probably too soon to be able to look back and reflect" on the impact the films have had on the public, Lawrence said.As for herself? "I hope I've grown up," added the star, who won an Oscar for her role in the 2012 comedy Silver Linings Playbook.Lawrence also addressed a recent blunt essay for an online feminist newsletter in which she blasted pay inequality between the sexes."I wasn't writing about not making as much as my male co-stars, as complaining about that I wasn't getting paid more because I'm a woman," she told reporters.In her post for Lenny, a newsletter co-founded by fellow actress Lena Dunham, Lawrence said that when she found out from Sony emails leaked last year that she was paid less than her male co-stars in the hit movie American Hustle, she didn't get mad at Sony but at herself.AdvertisementAdvertise with NZME.Lawrence, who topped Forbes magazine's 2015 list of best-paid actresses at US$52 million ($76.8 million), said that she loves what she does for a living."Honestly, it's a job," she said, acknowledging that "people are going to have opinions"."I really love acting, so I really just think of myself as a working woman," she added.• The Hunger Games: Mockingjay -
